# Finance

## Why it matters

Money is committed months before sponsorship and ticket income arrive.
A team that plans its cash flow keeps the trust of the venue, the Foundation and its sponsors.
See the how-to section for the steps.

## Applies when

- `size=medium,large` Smaller events can run on a simpler budget.
- `jurisdiction` Tax rules vary by country.

## Decisions you must make

- {bdg-danger}`MUST` (req: R-001; as-of: 2026-11-02) **Has the Foundation approved the conference name?** Ask the Board before you publish the name. (decide-by: T-12m)
- {bdg-primary}`DEFAULT` (basis: L-2002, L-2004) **Who sells the ticket?** Name the selling entity before pricing. (decide-by: T-9m)
- {bdg-secondary}`OPTION` **Do you offer a reduced ticket?** Decide from the budget sheet.

## How-to

1. Draft the budget sheet. Done when the treasurer shares the sheet with the team.
2. {bdg-secondary}`OPTION` Add a reserve line. Done when the reserve is in the sheet.

## Principles and general lessons

```{note} [general]
:class: hb-lesson hb-general
lesson | scope: general | source: S003 | ledger: L-2003 | confidence: observed | status: active | basis: structural | reason: The selling entity decides which tax rules apply to the ticket.

Name the selling entity before you set prices.
```

## Risks

```{note} Sponsor payments arrive after the venue deposit is due
:class: hb-risk hb-likelihood-medium hb-impact-high
risk | likelihood: medium | impact: high | mitigation: Agree a deposit schedule with the venue that follows the sponsor invoice dates. | owner-role: treasurer | playbook: venue-loss

The team carries the gap from its own reserve.
```
